editorial.editorial_title: Watching, reviewing, criticizing, doing, and choosing how to feel
editorial.summary: A 6:12 self-implicating monologue about replacing direct experience and creation with unboxings, game streams, reviews, criticism and negative media. Finishing Better Call Saul and crying leads immediately to review-seeking; borrowed judgment displaces making. The speaker stages an objection to himself, narrows claims to personal experience, and refuses an aggressive viral rant. Chili fries, a giant pot of plain quinoa, a bowel movement, murder documentaries, pornography, food and a stigmatizing crackhead simile supply intentionally bodily and provocative examples of wanting something but feeling bad afterward. Community support supplies the alternative. The close asks not only what one wants but how one wants to feel afterward. Every contradiction and detail remains; no behavioral, nutritional, therapeutic or addiction claim is invented.

connections.relationship: A strong Better Call Saul reaction is immediately displaced by reviews.
The music/architecture saying frames discussion as inferior to making.
A performed moral objection is followed by first-person narrowing.
Review consumption changes taste and displaces making.
Aggressive criticism is described as funny, entertaining and viral, then refused.
Chili fries illustrate desire followed by feeling bad.
Having only quinoa produces an unexpectedly positive food anecdote.
The speaker asks how consumption will feel afterward.
The crackhead comparison depicts seeking reviews that confirm negativity.
Mutual support supplies the positive-feeling counterexample.
Desired aftermath, not immediate want, is proposed as the decision input.
